tasks.short: Monitor facility use for rules, safety and order.

steps.what: Retrieve and check actual facility rules relevant to observed patron use
Monitor patrons' facility use to maintain rules, safety and order
inputs: actual patron behaviour and facility conditions
outputs: actual monitoring observations and personal intervention when required

tasks.design: Configure native topic links to actual house rules in {DOCS}. The attendant checks the relevant rule and personally monitors use and maintains safety and order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unfamiliar situations may require repeated rule navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native indexed house rules can shorten actual lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing unsafe conduct and responding appropriately require local awareness and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant understands the real situation and communicates with patrons.
tasks.altitude: Less rule lookup; monitoring stays fully retained.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: indexed facility rules can support lookup; they do not monitor patron conduct or replace safety intervention.

assumptions: Actual facility owner supplies current rules; attendant verifies relevance in s1. No model interprets behaviour or infers patron intent.

Boundary is actual rule lookup and monitoring. No record write, report or digital send is specified; actual incident recording or escalation must be decomposed separately before its work is estimated.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Only actual repeated unfamiliar-rule navigation is eligible; known rules and existing indexed lookup earn zero new saving.
unknowns: How often does the attendant actually look up rules?
research_questions: Can native rule links reduce lookup without changing monitoring coverage?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.50 rule navigation = 5; minus 0.5 upkeep = 4.5. Half eligible gives 2.5 minus 0.5 = 2. Monitoring and intervention stay fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.design: Configure native availability views and selected-space defaults in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The attendant checks actual availability, chooses an appropriate space, checks and commits the final allocation and personally hands over access.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments may repeat availability lookup and space/token entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native status views and exact selected-space reuse can reduce repetition.
tasks.still_hard: Actual availability, patron needs and correct key handoff require human checks.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant spots a space that is nominally free but unusable for the actual patron.
tasks.altitude: Less allocation entry; facility choice and handoff stay human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native facility allocation views can reuse recorded availability and selected-space fields; a recorded return alone does not establish physical usability.

assumptions: Actual prior assignment/return attendant supplies verified space identifier, status, event time and out-of-service flag. Current attendant verifies actual availability in retained s1; missing or stale status requires physical/manual checking.

Attendant chooses actual space and patron token in s2, captures missing allocation fields and checks exact final assignment in retained s3. No free return capture, key automation or self-service transfer is assumed.
Only existing allocation records are included; omit absent records and reweight. Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native functions first; existing configuration earns zero saving.
Routine commit retains one percent. Existing exact assignment check gates both commit and actual key handoff without added self-approval time. No actual key handoff is inferred from a record.
unknowns: Is availability reliably updated after actual returns?
research_questions: Can native availability/context reduce entry after actual space verification?

incremental.description: Maintain actual availability status and selected-space mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.50 lookup + 19*0.50 allocation entry = 19.5; minus 1 upkeep = 18.5. Half eligible gives 9.75 minus 1 = 8.75. Space choice, actual handoff and commit remain retained.

tasks.design: Configure native item/patron context in the existing issue record in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The attendant checks and physically issues the actual items, captures actual issued quantities and checks the final entry before committing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing issue records can repeat item and patron references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native selected-item context can reduce exact reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Correct size, condition and physical handoff require personal work.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant notices an item that is unsuitable or unsafe to issue.
tasks.altitude: Less issue-reference entry; handling stays intact.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native item context can reduce repeated issue-record references; a selected item is not proof of actual handoff.

assumptions: Attendant selects/checks actual items in s1, performs actual handoff in s2 and captures actual issued quantity and patron token in retained s3. No free scan, automatic handoff detection or planned-quantity record is assumed.
Only an existing issue record is included. If none exists, omit s3/s4 and reweight physical work: zero saving. No new tracking baseline is invented.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native context first; existing defaults earn zero saving. Routine commit retains one percent, and gates use existing item/record checks without extra self-approval work.
unknowns: Are these items actually recorded individually?
research_questions: Can native context reduce existing issue entry while preserving actual quantity capture?

approvals.approved_version: s1 checked exact actual selected items, quantities and patron token; changes require recheck
s3 checked final actual issue entry and exact item/patron record destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 9*0.20 repeated issue references = 1.8; minus 0.5 upkeep = 1.3. Half eligible gives 0.9 minus 0.5 = 0.4. Selection, physical issue, actual quantity capture and commit remain retained.

tasks.altitude: Less information lookup; customer explanation stays personal.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native facility information views can reduce source navigation; they do not replace customer clarification or establish unverified availability.

assumptions: Actual facility owner supplies current fees/policies and actual allocation/return records supply verified availability; attendant checks relevance and freshness in s1. Missing or stale information requires manual confirmation.
Boundary is lookup and oral explanation, with no record write, booking, payment or digital send required by this task. Actual additional transactions must be separately decomposed and gated.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Only actual repeated navigation is eligible; known answers and existing native views earn zero new saving. No generated policy is introduced.
